summary: Mali requires most visitors to obtain a visa, now applied for and paid online through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal, and the UK advises against all travel to the country. The ministry's visa check still waives the visa for most ECOWAS nationals despite Mali's January 2025 withdrawal from the bloc, but not for Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia or Sierra Leone; its Alliance of Sahel States partners Burkina Faso and Niger enjoy full free movement.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in Mali.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of arriving travelers and is checked at Bamako airport; it is also requested with visa applications.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Mali travel advice: entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but comprehensive coverage including medical evacuation is essential — care in Bamako is limited and evacuation from Mali is complicated by the security situation.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked, though visa applications ask for travel itineraries and airlines may ask for a return ticket.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers may ask visitors to show sufficient means for their stay.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency should be declared on arrival; limits apply to exporting CFA francs. Confirm the current rules with a Malian embassy before carrying large sums.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali

payments.text: Mali is a cash economy. Cards work only at a few Bamako hotels and banks. Bring euros to exchange (the CFA franc is pegged to the euro) and carry enough cash for your whole stay.

safety.text: Mali is run by a military junta and large areas are affected by jihadist insurgency and armed conflict. The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali: JNIM blockades on key routes, including around Bamako, target fuel trucks and travellers, overland routes to neighbouring countries are too dangerous, and the kidnapping threat extends to the capital.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Mali travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the cooler dry season and the only comfortable window — from March temperatures climb well above 40°C, and the June–September rains follow. Check security advice before planning any travel.

idp.text: Mali is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Mali is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Mali yet.

tips.text: The UK advises against all travel to the whole of Mali, including Bamako — terrorism, blockades on main roads and kidnapping are real risks. Take professional security advice before any trip.

Mali formally left ECOWAS in January 2025 together with Burkina Faso and Niger. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check still waives the visa for nationals of Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo, but asks those of Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone to apply. West African travelers should re-check shortly before traveling.
Do not photograph military personnel, checkpoints, government buildings or bridges — cameras and phones can be confiscated and detention is possible under the current military government.
Bring euros in cash. The CFA franc is pegged to the euro and exchanges easily in Bamako, while cards and ATMs cannot be relied on anywhere in the country.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Mali?
faq.answer: Most nationalities do. The application and payment are made online through the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal, and the entry permit is issued electronically; there is no tourist visa on arrival. Most ECOWAS nationals are still exempt (Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone are not), and citizens of Burkina Faso and Niger move freely under the Alliance of Sahel States.

faq.question: Is Mali safe to visit?
faq.answer: No — most Western governments advise against travel to all or most of Mali. Jihadist insurgency affects the north and center, attacks and kidnappings have reached areas near Bamako, and the country is governed by a military junta. Any travel needs serious security planning.

faq.question: Can ECOWAS citizens still enter Mali visa-free?
faq.answer: Most can. Although Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger formally withdrew from ECOWAS in January 2025, the Malian Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa check still tells nationals of Benin, Côte d'Ivoire, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria, Senegal and Togo that they need no visa. Nationals of Cape Verde, Ghana, Liberia and Sierra Leone are told a visa is required. The situation could change, so re-check shortly before travel.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Mali?
faq.answer: No. There is no routine tourist visa on arrival. Apply online before travel through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular portal (diplomatiemdc.gouv.ml), selecting the Malian embassy or consulate that covers your country of residence; the entry permit is issued electronically, with no need to send documents to the embassy.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Mali?
faq.answer: Yes. Carry an International Certificate of Vaccination. It is requested with visa applications and checked on arrival at Bamako-Sénou airport.
